chapter: California, New York and Richard Himber
title: First trip to California with Louis Prima, 1937
summary: Hirsch went to California with Prima in July 1937, hoping to earn a union membership for studio work, but they left in December.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I wanted to, if you're through with that, I wanted to ask you a question. Yeah. When did you first go to New York?

When did I first go to New York? Uh huh. I first went to California. Oh. Where was that? I first went to California. July the 17th, 1937. Uh huh. With Louis Prima. Louis Prima's band. And 1937, July 37. I went there with an ulterior motive. I don't think I ever told Louis about this, but it was an ulterior motive in the back of my mind. I had a lot of people that I had for, that I, if I was out there for six months, I could get to be a full member in the union. And I had a man by the name of Lou Forbes, who was at First National. I had a man by the name of Louis Forbes, who was at Warner Brothers. I had a guy by the name of Joe Cherniowski, who was at Columbia Pictures. And I had a man who was the drummer in the orchestra at 20th Century Fox, who told me that there was a chair waiting for me. If I ever got a, if I ever got a membership. So that's what I went out there for, to get a membership while I was working. Did you get it? We left December the 24th, right before. And that was the end of that. So I didn't get it. But I would have, if I had gotten a membership, I would have been back. I would probably be there today. Different, different world. But, uh.
